title: Benchmark for Safety Robustness Under Paraphrasing Attacks
original_idea: Generate 200 harmful prompts, then produce three paraphrase variants of each using an LLM. Evaluate three models on originals vs. paraphrases and measure the rate at which paraphrases succeed where originals fail.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If paraphrasing systematically circumvents safety measures, published safety scores drastically overestimate robustness. High practical relevance.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Using an LLM to generate paraphrases is simple. Running inference and comparing ASR is straightforward. Good beginner project.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 200 prompts x 3 paraphrases x 3 models = 2400 evaluations. The prompt generation is automated but 200 base prompts is ambitious to curate.

novelty.reasoning: Paraphrasing Adversarial Attack (PAA, arXiv:2601.06884, 2026) studies paraphrase-based attacks on LLM-as-a-reviewer but not on safety refusals specifically. General adversarial robustness benchmarks (PromptBench, AdvBench, AttackEval, RobustnessSuite) exist but do not focus specifically on paraphrase-based circumvention of safety measures with controlled experiments (original vs. paraphrase ASR comparison). The MLCommons Jailbreak Benchmark v0.5 includes some paraphrase-adjacent transformations but not a systematic paraphrase-only study. The specific experimental design — measuring the delta between original and paraphrased harmful prompt success rates — is a focused contribution not fully covered by existing work.

evidence: Paraphrasing Adversarial Attack on LLM-as-a-Reviewer. arXiv:2601.06884, 2026.
